sessions.phase_label: South Pointe performance diagnosis and security incident containment
South Pointe remediation, hardening, and speed optimization
Oak Bridge website recovery and malware remediation

requirements.title: South Pointe Visual Formatting Integrity
requirements.definition: Preserve or restore the legitimate fonts, styling, and page formatting of the South Pointe site during troubleshooting and optimization.
requirements.boundary_note: Visual integrity can regress independently of page speed and therefore remains separate from the performance Requirement.

requirements.title: South Pointe Unauthorized Account Removal
requirements.definition: Remove unauthorized South Pointe WordPress accounts while retaining only the client-designated legitimate administrators.
requirements.boundary_note: Account authorization has its own explicit retain/remove policy and can be completed independently of malicious-content or malware-code removal.

requirements.title: South Pointe Malicious Content Removal
requirements.definition: Remove unauthorized casino pages, posts, tags, and related malicious content from the South Pointe WordPress site.
requirements.boundary_note: On-site spam-content cleanup is independently observable and distinct from removing malware code, deleting accounts, and removing indexed URLs from search engines.

requirements.title: South Pointe Malware and Backdoor Removal
requirements.definition: Remove the malicious code, fake plugins, backdoors, and replicating infection responsible for the South Pointe compromise.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers eradication of the executable infection; spam records, unauthorized accounts, persistent monitoring, and search-index cleanup have separate acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: South Pointe Wordfence Protection
requirements.definition: Configure Wordfence to scan the South Pointe site and automatically detect or block future suspicious activity.
requirements.boundary_note: The persistent automated security control is an independently accepted operational behavior; short-term manual monitoring remains process evidence rather than another Requirement.

requirements.title: South Pointe Search-Index Spam Cleanup
requirements.definition: Submit the South Pointe malicious search-result URLs for removal so spam pages no longer damage search visibility and trust.
requirements.boundary_note: Search-engine cleanup is an external operational deliverable that can succeed or fail independently of deleting the corresponding content from WordPress.

requirements.title: South Pointe Compromised Credential Rotation
requirements.definition: Rotate South Pointe WordPress and WP Engine credentials and security keys following the compromise.
requirements.boundary_note: Credential rotation is a distinct access-control action and is not equivalent to removing unauthorized account records.

requirements.title: Oak Bridge Site Content and Layout Recovery
requirements.definition: Restore the Oak Bridge pages, posts, theme presentation, and visible site layout after the malware incident made content blank or unavailable.
requirements.boundary_note: The available evidence treats page availability and layout restoration as one coupled recovery outcome; malware eradication can proceed separately and therefore has its own Requirement.

requirements.title: Oak Bridge Malware and Backdoor Removal
requirements.definition: Remove malware, hacking backdoors, infected theme or plugin code, and other active compromise from the Oak Bridge site.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers eradication of the infection itself; restoring pages, removing accounts, configuring persistent protection, and search cleanup are independently testable sibling behaviors.

requirements.title: Oak Bridge Unauthorized Account Removal
requirements.definition: Remove hidden and unauthorized Oak Bridge administrator accounts while retaining only the client-designated legitimate account.
requirements.boundary_note: The client provides a site-specific account-retention rule, making this independent of malware-code and page restoration work.

requirements.title: Oak Bridge Wordfence Protection
requirements.definition: Configure Wordfence on Oak Bridge to scan for compromise and provide continuing protection against attacks.
requirements.boundary_note: Persistent security monitoring is separate from the one-time removal of the currently detected infection.

requirements.title: South Pointe Legacy Page-Load Performance
requirements.definition: Improve and maintain acceptable visitor-facing page-load performance for both the South Pointe legacy pages and the new RIB site experience.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the observable page-load outcome across both requested site contexts; image sizing, caching, fonts, plugins, and tracking scripts are diagnosis or implementation dimensions rather than independently client-managed outcomes here.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client tentatively suggests removing Thrive, but the legacy site still depends on it and the freelancer proposes deferring full removal while disabling only Thrive Apprentice. It is unclear whether full Thrive migration/removal became a confirmed Requirement.
Contact-form email delivery is identified as behavior that should be preserved after South Pointe remediation, but no client confirmation or observed test result establishes a clear lifecycle.
The freelancer identifies a potentially incorrect Stape Conversion Tracking container URL, but the client does not resolve whether the configuration is intentional before wrapping up.

Oak Bridge private-page and contact-form functionality could constitute narrower preservation Requirements, but the supplied history contains only requests for client testing and no target-specific observed outcomes.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Chris, here's the full rundown after a day of digging.

It turned out to be more than the fake admin users we spotted last night. There was also a hidden admin account buried in the database, along with around 470 casino spam pages published under it. Code planted inside one of your plugins was keeping all of it invisible, and it was also messing with the site's caching, which is why pages were taking 15+ seconds to load for visitors.

Everything is cleaned up now. About 7 hours all in today:
\- Removed the hidden admin account and all ~470 spam pages
\- Swapped the tampered plugin for a fresh official copy
\- Reinstalled WordPress itself
\- Worked with WP Engine to reset the site's credentials and keys, and I've requested a full platform-level malware scan for independent confirmation
\- Set up Wordfence as a security scanner that will alert us if anything suspicious happens again

The result: pages now load in under 2 seconds instead of 16, and I'm keeping an eye on things for the next couple of days to make sure it stays clean.

A few things I need from you:
1\. The security reset logged everyone out of WordPress. When you log back in, set a new password, and have any other admins do the same
2\. Change your WP Engine password too, just to be safe
3\. Add me to your Google Search Console so I can get the spam pages out of Google before they hurt your rankings. Settings > Users and permissions > Add user > Full access, using this email: ken@nexxdigital.my
4\. Send a quick test through your contact form and make sure the email comes through, just to confirm your leads are still flowing after all the changes

Still on my list:
\- Search Console cleanup once I'm in
\- Update your outdated plugins (probably how they got in originally)
\- Share WP Engine's scan results when they come back

Happy to answer any questions, and I can send over a proper written report if you'd like one for your records.
